proposal: The Mandate recommends that BIS act unilaterally to tighten Export Administration Regulations for countries of concern such as China and Russia, reversing 2008 to 2016 loosening. Listed steps include moving toward more restrictive country groups, ending license exceptions, broadening foreign direct product rules, lowering the de minimis threshold, tightening deemed-export and fundamental-research rules, adding many more companies to the Entity List, and denying licenses where end-use checks are blocked.
remaining: Decide whether the affiliates rule resumes on 2026-11-10 or is extended; a commentary page reported announced extension plans to 2027-01-10 but no Federal Register extension as of 2026-10-03.

Rules on de minimis thresholds, foreign direct product reach, deemed exports, fundamental research, license exceptions and 'specially designed' items: no action found in BIS Federal Register documents since 2025-01-20.
Redesignation of China and Russia to more restrictive country groups: no action found.

Open nomination process for emerging and foundational technology controls, equal agency votes in license disputes, and quarterly license data to Congress: no related BIS document found in the Federal Register review (not exhaustively checked).

Entity List treatment of apps such as TikTok and WeChat: a Federal Register search of BIS documents for those names since 2025-01-20 returned nothing. A Justice Department rule on restricting bulk data transfers to countries of concern (published 2025-01-08 under Executive Order 14117) is a parallel measure of different design, not the BIS-implemented executive order the Mandate describes.

status_summary: BIS has issued rules in both directions. Tightening steps include large Entity List additions in 2025 (two rules on 2025-03-28 covering about 80 entities, most under China; 32 entries on 2025-09-16, 23 of them under China; 26 entities and 3 addresses on 2025-10-09), removal of validated end-user status for three China chip plants (effective 2025-12-31), and a 2025-09-30 interim final rule (90 FR 47201) extending Entity List restrictions to entities 50 percent or more owned by listed parties. That affiliates rule has been suspended since 2025-11-10 (90 FR 50857) as part of a U.S.-China trade arrangement announced by the White House on 2025-11-01; the suspension runs through 2026-11-09, and a Federal Register query of BIS documents published from 2026-09-01 shows no extension, with no BIS documents listed after 2026-09-30. Loosening steps include a 2026-01-15 rule (91 FR 1684) moving licenses for certain advanced AI chips to end-users located in China or Macau from presumed denial to case-by-case review, while other D:5 destinations and Macau-headquartered entities stay under presumed denial, and an August 2026 rule easing controls on drones with under three hours of endurance. BIS's Entity List rules in 2026 removed entries (two Hong Kong addresses and one entity listed under Turkey, both on 2026-08-24) and added none, and BIS Federal Register documents since 2025-01-20 include no rule on de minimis, foreign direct product, deemed export, fundamental research or country-group changes.

timeline.event: BIS publishes two Entity List rules. One adds 12 entities (11 in China, one in Taiwan) for supercomputing and military-modernization links; the second adds 70 entries (68 unique entities), 42 of them under China and the rest mainly Pakistan, the UAE, South Africa and Iran. This link is the larger rule; the 12-entity rule is cited under sources.

BIS removes validated end-user authorizations for three China-based chip plants (Intel Dalian, Samsung China Semiconductor, SK hynix China), effective 2025-12-31, and estimates about 1,000 additional license applications a year as a result.
BIS adds 32 entries to the Entity List, 23 of them under China, citing military space, quantum, semiconductor-equipment diversion and circumvention concerns; also corrects 27 existing entries.
BIS interim final rule (90 FR 47201) extends Entity List and similar end-user restrictions automatically to entities at least 50 percent owned by listed parties.

BIS adds 29 entries (26 entities and 3 addresses) to the Entity List, 19 of them under China including Hong Kong, mainly for supplying components to Iranian-linked drone programs; 9 Turkish entities and one UAE entity are also added.

BIS publishes a final rule staying the affiliates rule for one year (90 FR 50857), effective 2025-11-10 through 2026-11-09, after which the provisions resume on 2026-11-10 unless extended. The White House fact sheet of 2025-11-01 on a U.S.-China arrangement listed the suspension among U.S. steps.

BIS final rule (91 FR 1684) moves license review for advanced computing chips below set performance thresholds (such as Nvidia H200 and AMD MI325X class) from presumption of denial to case-by-case when destined to end-users located in China or Macau, subject to certification, a 50 percent cap relative to U.S. shipments, security and third-party testing conditions; other D:5 destinations, reexports and transfers to Macau, and entities headquartered in Macau or D:5 stay under presumption of denial.

BIS final rule raises the endurance threshold for national security controls on drones from one hour to three hours and removes those controls on related software and technology for lesser drones, describing the change as supporting U.S. drone industry competitiveness; it builds on a January 2026 interim final rule and leaves those changes in place.

title: Tighten export controls on China and expand Entity List restrictions
uncertainties: The Federal Register review used rule titles plus fetched summaries of the Entity List and export rules named above; BIS rules whose titles were not opened (for example the 2025-12-05 Commerce Control List rule) could contain provisions not seen. The affiliates-rule extension status rests on one commentary page that itself relies on press reports of statements by Treasury and China's commerce ministry, not on a Federal Register notice or a White House document; the 2026-09-25 White House fact sheet on a China state visit does not mention export controls. Entity List counts are taken from the rules' own text as summarized by a fetch tool and should be rechecked against the notices. Reasons for the affiliates suspension are stated by the White House as part of a broader arrangement; the Federal Register notice itself gives none. Not checked: Russia-related listings, the status of the 2025 AI diffusion framework, and total Entity List counts. The suspension rule (90 FR 50857) and the chip rule (91 FR 1684) were re-read on federalregister.gov in this review; the chip rule's case-by-case policy covers end-users located in China or Macau, while Macau reexports and transfers and Macau-headquartered entities stay under presumption of denial. The Federal Register API listing fetched on 2026-10-17 showed no BIS documents after 2026-09-30, which may reflect indexing lag. The distinct-entity count in the 2025-09-16 Entity List rule (29 or 30) was not settled from the page read on 2026-10-23, so the event gives the entry count only.
